issues.display_title: Issue #826: feat(preview): trip summary and step modal, incl. the small-screen map coexistence (#779)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-826-steps-surface.mp4

Source PRD: #779 · Design: #782 · Design branch: design/multi-place-direction

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

The trip summary block and the step modal, including the thing the PRD called the hard one: the modal must not cover the map while a step is selected on a phone. R45-R51, R70-R78. Depends on #823; overlaps #824's panel layout.

Scope

Summary

Port src/components/editor/preview/TripSummaryCard.tsx (165 lines, incl. STATUS_COPY and legFailureReason). Origin, place count, total distance, total time, floor changes, building count — zero values omitted, not rendered as zero (R45-R51, D10). The unscaled variant drops distance and time entirely: no placeholder, no warning (R59).

Step modal

Port src/components/editor/preview/TripStepsPanel.tsx (285 lines, plus the SelectedStepBar export at :208). Leg group headings ("2. Bank"), internal scrolling, step count shown on the opening control (R70-R74). Step selection wires through to the map focus logic that already exists from #793.

Small screens (D13 / R77, R78)

The design branch already answers this — SelectedStepBar is that answer. Take the pattern it implements rather than re-deciding it, and confirm whether desktop uses the same one.

Reconcile with what development already built

The design branch was cut at 90f1997, before #792 / #793 / #794 merged. It carries src/components/editor/preview/RouteSteps.tsx (177 lines) — the pre-merge sibling of development's RouteResult.tsx, which now owns the same job (status, summary, step timeline, step selection, and #794's compact layout). Do not add both. TripSummaryCard / TripStepsPanel must sit on RouteResult.tsx and the routeSteps.ts / routeDistance.ts primitives development already has (see #823), with RouteSteps.tsx dropped.

Panel width is a real decision here: DirectionPanel.tsx is a fixed max-w-[300px] column, and place list + summary + modal trigger have to fit a phone alongside #794's compact route layout (R11, D11).

Tests

Summary omits zero values; unscaled project renders no distance/time; step count on the trigger matches the step list; leg grouping headings; a selected step keeps the map visible at phone width.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

RESULT

Branch: feature/826-trip-summary-steps · PR: #837 (merged) · Commit: 3929bfe

The steps take the Direction panel's slot and the place list steps aside — one column, one thing in it. TripSummaryCard stays behind as the door to them: origin, place count, the total when there is an honest one, and a control that says how many steps it opens.

That is also the answer to open question Q6. Nothing overlays the map, because this surface sits in the panel's corner rather than the map's; the list highlights the selected row and stays put, and SelectedStepBar at the foot of the map names the step being read with previous / next / clear.

Grouped by leg out here: each group headed by the place it ends at and that place's number, each leg's first instruction starting at the place before it. A failed leg is marked in place, and the legs after it keep their numbers and their steps.

RouteResult was replaced rather than kept alongside — two surfaces drawing the same steps drift apart. Its step row, icons and wording moved to RouteStepRow; its formatters to routeDistance. tripStepList is now the single flattening of a trip's steps, so the list, the bar and the camera cannot disagree about which leg a step belongs to.

Tests: TripSummaryCard.test.tsx (14), TripStepsPanel.test.tsx (20), DirectionPanel.test.tsx rewritten (7), PreviewOverlay.routeStepSelect.test.tsx updated. Demo .playwright-mcp/demo/826/video-826-steps-surface.mp4 (89s) asserts on camera that the surface never reaches across the map, before and after a step is selected.

issues.display_title: Issue #827: feat(preview): partial trips, and replan clearing step selection (#779)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-827-replan.mp4

Source PRD: #779 · Design: #782 · Design branch: design/multi-place-direction

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

A trip where one leg fails is still a trip. R81-R91. Depends on #823, #826. Last task of the Direction half.

Scope

Partial trips

  • Per-leg status on the trip model (TripLeg already carries the field from #823).
  • A failed leg suppresses the totals and every arrival time downstream of it; arrival times upstream stay (R83-R87).
  • The place beyond a failed leg still shows its number and its marker — a partial trip is not an erased trip (R86, D16).
  • A failed leg must not read as "the whole trip errored" (D16). legFailureReason in TripSummaryCard.tsx:24 is the copy seam.
  • All legs fail → fall back to the existing single-route failure behaviour, unchanged (R91).

Replan and step selection

  • Any replan clears the step selection (R81).
  • An open step modal updates in place rather than closing (R82).

Tests

Upstream arrivals kept / downstream suppressed; totals suppressed on any failure; numbering and markers survive past a failed leg; all-legs-fail falls back to the existing failure path; replan clears selection; open modal updates in place.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

RESULT

Branch: feature/827-partial-trips · PR: #838 (merged) · Commit: 17af7e5

A trip whose second leg had no route drew nothing at all: both map gates asked the concatenated route for status === "found", and a trip takes the first failure's status. One unreachable stop erased the leg the visitor could actually walk. The gates read the segments now — every non-found status returns none, so a failed single route still draws nothing, and a leg that routed is drawn whatever became of the ones after it.

Also fixed: the summary quoted the failure reason lower-cased into its sentence, turning "No door in Beta" into a building nobody has.

The rest of #827 was already true by construction and is now covered rather than assumed — totals and downstream arrivals withheld (#823), the failed leg marked in place (#826), replan clearing the step selection (#793 identity guard), and the open steps surface re-rendering from the new trip.

PreviewOverlay.partialTrip.test.tsx (9 cases) drives the real component against a two-building project where one building has no door.

Demo .playwright-mcp/demo/827/video-827-replan.mp4 (91s) covers the replan rules. The partial-trip half is deliberately not filmed: every place in the demo project can be reached from every other, so there is no honest way to make a leg fail on camera — the test above is what covers it.

issues.display_title: Issue #840: fix(editor): Import Editable TXT is dropped when the selected building has no floor
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-840-import-no-floor.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Found while tracing #786 (closed as a duplicate of #795). Same symptom — an import that appears to do nothing — but a different path and a different cause, so it survived that fix.

Repro. In a project whose selected building has no floors (a building just added, or one whose floors were all deleted): Project → Import Editable TXT → pick a floorplan .txt. Nothing appears, nothing is saved, and reloading shows the project exactly as it was. Dragging the same .txt onto the canvas does the same.

Cause. Both of those paths hand the file straight to the engine:

  • src/components/editor/EditorTopbar.tsx:399 — f.text().then((t) => engine?.loadText(t, f.name))
  • src/components/editor/FloorplanEditor.tsx:617-620 — handleFloorplanFile, wired to the canvas onDrop at :690

The engine then raises change, and the store write bails at src/components/editor/FloorplanEditor.tsx:349:

const id = activeIdRef.current; // scoped (#536): no level in this building = no cursor broadcast
if (!id) return;

activeIdRef is null exactly when the selected building holds no level, so the geometry lives in the engine and never reaches canvasData. Autosave has nothing to persist, floorConfigs gains no floor, and EditorCanvas keeps the surface hidden because floorsPresent is false — so the import is invisible as well as unsaved.

The guard itself is right: #536 put it there so nothing is ever written under a synthetic DEFAULT_LEVEL_ID, which is what spawned the phantom "level-1" entries. The bug is that two callers reach the engine without giving it a level to write to.

Two paths already do this correctly, and are the model to follow — both mint a level first and go through the store:

  • EmptyProjectPlaceholder.tsx:41 (the empty-project dropzone, #454): appendTxtLevel → addFloorConfig → setCanvasData → setActiveLevelId
  • add-level/useAddLevel.ts:146 (Add Floor → Import, #455): the same, for a MapThru floorplan .txt

Scope

Fix it once, where both callers route through, rather than in each caller: an import that arrives with no level to write to should create the level it needs, exactly as those two paths do, and the same guard should keep protecting everything else.

Decide deliberately whether the new floor is named from the file (originalFileName) or from defaultFloorName(nextFloorSequence(...)) — the two working paths differ, and the wrong choice here shows up in the floor list.

Also worth settling: a drop or an import while a level IS active replaces that level's geometry today. That is the intended "import editable txt" behaviour and should not change — only the no-level case is broken.

Tests

An import with no level in the selected building creates one, lands in canvasData, and marks the store dirty; an import with a level active still replaces that level rather than adding a second; the created level is stamped with the selected building (#536).

Notes

Not reachable from a project with zero floors overall in the same way — there the canvas surface is hidden and the empty-project card offers its own (working) dropzone. The building-with-no-floors case is the one that reaches the broken path.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

RESULT

Branch: feature/840-import-txt-no-floor · PR: #842 (merged) · Commit: 1f8078f

mintLevel in FloorplanEditor.tsx gives a change with nowhere to go a floor of its own — the same thing the empty-project dropzone (#454) and Add Floor's txt import (#455) do, placed in the one seam both broken callers (and a first stroke drawn on an empty building) pass through.

It refuses where a floor must not be invented: a remote apply, an empty model (the engine clears itself on mount, floor switch and destroy), and a viewer.

The floor is named Floor N counted within the selected building rather than after the file — the two working paths disagreed, and the floor list, the 3D stack and the picker are all counting. It is also framed on the first frame it is visible for: the surface is hidden while a building has no floor, so the camera had never been near that geometry and the import appeared parked in a corner.

FloorplanEditor.importNoFloor.test.tsx (7 cases) drives the real change callback through a stubbed engine. Demo .playwright-mcp/demo/840/video-840-import-no-floor.mp4 (68s): a building with no floors → one import → Floor 1, 54 objects, framed in 2D and 3D, "Saved just now".

issues.display_title: Issue #843: fix(auth): read the support role live, so the sidebar and the guard cannot disagree
issues.main_description_html:
Source report: #785 · Related: #583 (same subject, read path still open) · Backend: GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#121

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

The dashboard offers a Support link that bounces straight back to the dashboard. Two things decide "is this user support", and they read from different places:

Decides Reads Freshness
whether the sidebar shows Support DashboardSidebar → useUserStore → getMeAction() → GET /v1/auth/me (src/actions/projects.ts:220-237) live
whether /support opens session.user.role ← token.role (src/proxy.ts:52-56, src/app/support/page.tsx:24) frozen at sign-in

token.role is written once at sign-in (src/auth.ts:90 credentials, :116 Google) and refreshed only when something calls session.update() (src/auth.ts:43 → refreshFromMe). The one caller in the app is verify-email (verify-email-client.tsx:56). The session TTL is 30 days.

So a user granted the support role after their last sign-in sees the link — /v1/auth/me says support — and is refused by both guards, which are reading a token minted before the grant. That is the report: the link is visible, hovering shows /support, clicking lands back on /dashboard.

The mirror case is the more serious one. A revoked support role keeps working for up to 30 days, because nothing re-reads it. That is exactly what the design set out to prevent — src/lib/support/sessionRole.ts says so in its own header:

The role is deliberately NOT carried in the JWT. The session token has a 30-day TTL, so an embedded role would keep revoked support access alive for up to a month — it is always read from GET /v1/auth/me instead.

The write path was fixed in da956ba (#583). The read path still caches.

Scope

Make the guard read the role the same way the sidebar does, so the two cannot disagree in either direction.

Resolve the role from /v1/auth/me (using session.accessToken) in the proxy for /support paths only — that is the only place a role is used, and /start, /editor and /dashboard run through the same proxy on every request and must not pay for a call they never read. src/app/support/page.tsx should resolve it the same way rather than trusting the session, so a direct hit on the route is checked too.

hasSupportAccess and roleFrom stay as they are; what changes is where the role comes from.

Decide deliberately what a failed /v1/auth/me means here. Both answers are defensible and they are not the same:

  • refuse — a support page nobody can open during an API outage
  • fall back to the cached token role — an outage extends whatever the token last said

Whichever is picked, say so in a comment where the decision lives: this is an access-control path and the next reader should not have to infer it.

If the call is worth caching, cache it with a short TTL on the token (roleCheckedAt), not with ?? — ?? is the bug #583 already fixed once.

Tests

/support opens for a user whose /v1/auth/me says support but whose token does not; /support refuses a user whose token says support but whose /v1/auth/me no longer does (the revocation case); /dashboard, /start and /editor do not fetch /v1/auth/me in the proxy; a failed /v1/auth/me behaves the way the decision above states. src/__tests__/proxy-access-control.test.ts is where the proxy's rules are already covered.

Notes

Not reproducible with a session that was created after the role was granted — the dev account here already carries role: "support" in its session and /support opens normally. Reproduce by granting the role to an account that is already signed in, or by clearing the role on the backend for a signed-in support user (the revocation case, which needs no new grant at all).

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

RESULT

Branch: feature/843-live-support-role · PR: #844 (merged) · Commit: 94213b2

hasLiveSupportAccess(accessToken) in src/lib/support/sessionRole.ts asks GET /v1/auth/me at the moment of the decision. Both guards use it — src/proxy.ts for the route, src/app/support/page.tsx for a direct hit on it — so the sidebar and the gate can no longer disagree in either direction.

Two decisions, both commented where they live:

  • An unreachable /v1/auth/me refuses, rather than falling back to the token's copy. It is an access-control answer, so the safe direction for an unknown one is no — and it costs nothing real, because the support dashboard's contents come from that same API.
  • Scoped to /support, the only path where a role decides anything. The same proxy runs on /start, /editor and /dashboard on every request and none of them reads a role; there is a test that they make no call.

Tests: sessionRole.test.ts +6 (grant, revocation, failed and thrown API, no token, no caching), proxy-access-control.test.ts +5 (stale-session grant let in, stale-session revocation refused, unreachable API refused, other protected paths pay nothing, signed-out still goes to login). Checked against the running app: /support opens for a real support session and lists its feedback.

No demo video — the fix only shows itself in a session state that cannot be staged locally, and the guard runs server-side so the browser cannot answer for /v1/auth/me.

issues.display_title: Issue #848: fix(editor): Convert To Room reads an imported Area's closed ring as a self-intersection
issues.main_description_html:
Reported in-session with a screenshot on project 23839d5f-5390-45e8-9cb1-3109bf7d65d8 (Mappedin mall import): Convert To Room refuses. Sibling of #839, which introduced the command. The refusal has two independent causes; this is the first. The second is the sibling task on room-detection resolution.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

convertAreaToRoom (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/commands.ts:215) validates the Area's polygon with isSimplePolygon before it generates a wall per edge, and refuses a self-crossing one — a figure-eight would produce a wall set enclosing nothing (PRD §7). The check is right; its ring convention is not.

Everything drawn in the editor leaves a ring open (finishArea pushes the traced points and stops). Everything imported arrives closed — Mappedin repeats the first vertex at the end. isSimplePolygon (src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts:393) skips only the edge pairs that are adjacent in an open ring:

if (j === i || j === i + 1 || (i === 0 && j === n - 1)) continue;

On a closed ring the last real edge ends exactly where edge 0 begins, and that pair is not skipped. segmentsCross returns true for two segments sharing an endpoint when the far point falls on one side — its own doc claims otherwise, but the adjacency skip is what has been carrying that promise:

c=(0,0) d=(1,0) a=(1,0) b=(1,1)   d1=0 d2=1 d3=1 d4=0  ->  true

So an imported Area is read as self-intersecting and refused with "this area crosses itself — reshape it before converting to a room", which is not what is wrong with it.

Measured on the reported project

Level 1 of 23839d5f: 23597 × 19598 units, 12 walls, 269 manual Areas, 267 of them with a duplicated closing vertex.

as shipped ring normalised
refused "crosses itself" 214 1 (a genuinely self-crossing ring)
refused "couldn't build a room" 39 221 — the sibling task
converts 16 47

Level 2 (401 Areas) goes from 0 convertible to 56.

Scope

Normalise the ring once, where both the validator and the wall generator read it, rather than guarding each reader: consecutive duplicates dropped cyclically, at the same 0.5-unit tolerance convertAreaToRoom already applies when it decides an edge is too short to be a wall. That way the polygon that is validated is exactly the polygon that becomes walls.

Do not "fix" this by loosening segmentsCross to ignore touching endpoints — a ring that pinches through a shared vertex would then pass.

Tests

A closed square ring is simple; the escalator ring from the reported project is simple; a bow-tie is still rejected, closed or open; a ring that collapses to fewer than 3 corners is rejected; Convert To Room on a closed-ring Area produces one wall per corner (not one extra zero-length wall) and carries the Area's name onto the Room. src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/__tests__/geometry.test.ts and src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/convert-area-to-room.test.ts.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

RESULT

Branch: feature/848-closed-ring-area · PR: #855 (merged) · Commit: 7ca0a9c · in main via #857

ringCorners in src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts reduces a ring to the corners a wall builder would use — consecutive duplicates dropped cyclically, at the same 0.5-unit tolerance convertAreaToRoom already applied when deciding an edge was too short to be a wall. isSimplePolygon and convertAreaToRoom both read that one list, so the polygon that is validated is exactly the polygon that becomes walls; the inline zero-length skip in the edge loop is gone.

segmentsCross was left alone on purpose. Loosening it to ignore touching endpoints would also let through a ring that pinches through a shared vertex.

Convertible Areas on 23839d5f: 16 → 47 on level 1, 0 → 56 on level 2. The rest were still refused by detection resolution — that is #849, which landed on top of this.

Tests: geometry.test.ts (closed square simple, the reported project's escalator ring simple, bow-tie still rejected closed or open, ring collapsing under 3 corners rejected, duplicates anywhere dropped) and convert-area-to-room.test.ts (a closed-ring Area converts, one wall per corner, name carried onto the Room).

pnpm test 208 files / 1891 pass · pnpm lint 0 errors · tsc --noEmit clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #849: fix(editor): room detection cannot resolve a room that is small relative to the plan
issues.main_description_html:
Second half of the Convert To Room refusal reported on project 23839d5f-5390-45e8-9cb1-3109bf7d65d8 — the half that produced the screenshot's actual message, "couldn't build a room from this area — the area is unchanged". The first half is the sibling task on closed rings. This one is not a Convert bug: Convert is only the first feature to hit it.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

detectRooms (src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/rooms.ts:22) rasterizes the walls onto a grid whose longest side is a fixed 300 cells:

const scale = Math.min(1, 300 / Math.max(model.w, model.h, 1));

then dilates every wall pixel 3×3, flood-fills the gaps, and discards any region under 12 cells. On a plan a few hundred units across that is fine. On the reported project the plan is 23597 × 19598 units, so one cell is 79 units, and:

feature size cells across detected
Walmart 5313 u 67 yes
Urban Planet 979 u 12 yes
Escalators 249 u 3.1 no
Elevators 84 u 1.1 no
WOW! mobile boutique 55 u 0.7 no

Wall dilation eats a cell on each side, so anything under roughly 5 cells encloses nothing at all. With the ring fix in place, 221 of 269 Areas on level 1 and 344 of 401 on level 2 still cannot be converted.

This is not specific to Convert To Room. Drawing those same walls by hand on this plan produces no Room either — the raster cannot see the loop however it got there. Convert is simply the first command that says so out loud.

Scope

Make room detection resolve a room whose size is small relative to the plan. Two directions, both measured on the reported project (median detectRooms, which recomputeRooms runs on every model change):

raster cap convertible of 269 ms per edit
300 (today) 47 18
600 80 42
900 119 69
1200 164 154
1800 226 353
  1. Raise the cap adaptively — cheap, and bounded: 900 is about as far as it goes before a drag stutters, and it still leaves more than half the mall unconvertible. A stop-gap, not an answer.
  2. Detect rooms from the wall graph instead of the raster — build the planar graph of wall segments and take its minimal cycles as rooms. Resolution-independent, so a 2.75 m kiosk on a 1.1 km plan detects exactly like a room on a house plan, and on this data it is far cheaper than the raster it replaces. Room polygons come out of the graph exactly, which also retires the wall-hugging/snapping pass that exists only to undo raster error.

Direction 2 is the fix; pick it unless the measurement says otherwise. Note that its blast radius is real and must be checked before it lands: detectRooms output feeds room polygons, 3D extrusion, the persisted level (modelToLevel), and the map/preview surfaces. Any isolated closed wall loop — a column drawn as a box — becomes a Room under cycle detection where the raster used to swallow it.

Whichever direction, the refusal message should stay honest for the case that genuinely cannot be built: the current wording is right, it was just being reached for the wrong reason.

Related

Converting many Areas on this project pushes the model to ~5100 walls, and detectRooms then takes ~2.5 s per call regardless of raster size — wallsOnPolygon is O(walls × regions × polygon). Independent of this task, but it is the next wall the same project runs into, and direction 2 changes that cost too.

Tests

A room small relative to the plan is detected (the reported project's escalator ring on a 23597-unit plan); an existing house-scale plan detects the same rooms as before, with the same polygons; Convert To Room succeeds on an Area that the 300-cell raster could not resolve. src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/__tests__/rooms.test.ts holds the detection cases.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

RESULT

Branch: feature/849-room-detection-scale · PR: #856 (merged) · Commit: cbb302a · in main via #857

Direction 2 (wall-graph cycles) was not taken. Direction 1 (raise the cap) was measured and rejected. What shipped is a third one: reframe instead of refine.

detectIn(model, wallIds, ox, oy, fw, fh) spends its 300 cells on whatever box it is handed, and detectRooms hands it two:

  1. the whole plan — the pass that has always run, unchanged;
  2. then each group of end-to-end connected walls that holds a cycle and that pass 1 put no room inside, framed on its own bounding box. 300 cells across a kiosk resolves the kiosk.

Pass 2 only appends, after pass 1, rooms nothing had found — so no existing room changes polygon, centroid, d:cx:cy key (its height) or array position (areaMeta in recomputeRooms), and none is found twice.

Two decisions worth naming, both commented where they live:

  • Groups with no cycle never reach the raster (connected graph, |E| >= |V|). Only a cycle can bound a room. Without this the mall's own outline walls each paid for a plan-sized raster — it was measurably the difference between 93 ms and 70 ms on the first conversion, and much more later.
  • The skip test asks where the rooms landed, not which walls they touched. A loop small enough to sit inside a detected region has its walls voted onto that region and would look "covered" while enclosing nothing of its own.

Effect, converting each Area in turn on 23839d5f

before with #848 with this
level 1 (269 Areas) 16 47 245
level 2 (401 Areas) 0 56 389

detectRooms on that project as it stands: ~10 ms, unchanged. Remaining failures: 24 sub-unit Areas (below one cell even framed alone) and one genuinely self-crossing ring.

Left open, deliberately

  • A small room inside a large connected wall network is still missed — its group is the whole network. Ending the resolution question outright still means the wall-graph rewrite described above; this stopped at the case that reaches users, an imported plan of separate footprints.
  • Detection still costs O(rooms × walls) — ~2.8 s once a model carries 4000 walls. Pre-existing, listed under "Related" above, and now easier to reach because converting works. Worth its own task.

Not exercised in the browser against the reported project: the editor autosaves two seconds after a change, and converting there would edit the reporter's own data. Verified against that project's real persisted state, replayed through the shipped code path, plus unit tests.

Tests: rooms.test.ts — a kiosk-sized loop on a mall-sized plan is found once with a centroid inside it; two loops give two rooms; a name override lands on a reframed room; a room pass 1 already found is not reported twice; open chains and crossing stubs invent nothing; a sub-unit loop is still nothing.

pnpm test 208 files / 1891 pass · pnpm lint 0 errors · tsc --noEmit clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #850: fix(preview): Nearby asks where a place is on the ground, not where its marker is drawn (#789)
issues.main_description_html:
Follow-up to #847 (PRD #789) · Branch the work carries: feature/789-viewer-search-discovery

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Nearby decides what is on screen by projecting each object's anchor with map.project(lngLat) and testing the result against the canvas box (src/lib/preview/nearbyTargets.ts). map.project takes a lng/lat and nothing else, so every anchor is projected as if it sat on the ground.

The markers those anchors describe are not on the ground. MapObjectMarkers — which the viewer mounts too (PreviewOverlay.tsx:1115) — positions each one at MercatorCoordinate.fromLngLat([lng, lat], altitude) with the altitude from levelBaseHeights, then projects through the map's own matrix in a custom-layer render callback.

On the ground floor the two agree. Higher up they do not: at the default 49° pitch, a floor eight storeys up is roughly a screen-height's worth of offset, so a place whose marker is drawn well inside the view has its ground point off the top edge — and Nearby drops it. The mirror case admits places the visitor cannot see. Nearby is meant to be exactly the set someone could have tapped on the map instead of opening Search, and above the ground floor it is not that set.

Scope

The lazy answer is probably not to reproduce the projection. MapObjectMarkers already computes, every frame, at the right altitude, which markers are on screen — it culls off-screen buttons for performance (reposition, the pass-1 coarse cull). That is the same question Nearby is asking, answered correctly, once.

Have it publish the on-screen id set and let useNearbyTargets consume that in place of its own projection, which would delete the computeCoordSpace / makeLevelPixelTransform / pixelToLngLat chain from nearbyTargets.ts entirely.

Two things to settle before committing to that:

It repositions per animation frame, so the set cannot go into React state as it changes — that is a render per frame. Publish through a ref and notify on settle (moveend, resize), which is the cadence useNearbyTargets already recomputes on.

Check the marker set actually covers every search kind. computeMarkerAnchors emits area, door, point, safety, access, rect, circle and polygon; search targets are area, point, shape, safety, access. If MapObjectMarkers filters by its visibility props or by link state in a way that would hide a searchable place, the published set has to be the pre-filter one — an object being unlabelled on the map does not stop it being a place.

If that coupling turns out worse than the duplication, the fallback is to project in nearbyTargets.ts the same way the markers do: MercatorCoordinate.fromLngLat([lng, lat], levelBaseHeights(...)) and the map's projection matrix. Say in a comment which was chosen and why.

Nearby still orders by distance from the middle of the view, and still dedupes by Information record after the containment test — that ordering is what makes R19 work (see #847).

Tests

src/lib/preview/__tests__/useNearbyTargets.test.tsx fakes the camera already; extend it so a place on an upper floor whose marker is on screen is listed, and one whose marker is off screen is not — the case that fails today. Keep the existing coverage of when the list recomputes.

Notes

Not a regression: Nearby is new in #789. This is the accuracy of a new list, not the loss of an old one.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

issues.display_title: Issue #851: fix(preview): on a phone the Information card buries the Search panel it was opened from (#789)
issues.main_description_html:
Follow-up to #847 (PRD #789) · Branch the work carries: feature/789-viewer-search-discovery

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

#789 removed the activeFeature !== "search" gate that hid the Information card while Search was open. That was right on a desktop — the two stopped sharing the top-right slot long ago, and picking a place out of Nearby only to be told nothing about it is the worse bug (R45).

On a phone they share the whole screen. At 390px the card spans x=24..334 and the panel x=16..374, and the card is taller than panelTop, so tapping a Nearby row buries the search input and the entire result list underneath it. The card comes later in the DOM and wins, which is the right answer to a tap and the wrong picture to be left with: the list the visitor was reading is gone, and nothing says how to get it back. They collide below roughly 964px — the panel is min(380px, 100vw-2rem) and the card is 512px.

The PRD asks for this explicitly (§8, mobile usability: "Visitor can use default, active search, category, and recent sections on a phone without layout overflow").

Scope

There is already a house answer to two panels wanting one surface, from #779: the steps take this slot and the place list steps aside, so a selected step is never read around the map it points at. Do the same here — on a narrow viewport the card takes the surface and the Search panel steps aside, coming back when the card is dismissed.

That keeps the mobile flow honest: you tapped a place, you read it, you close it, you are back in the list. Suppressing the card instead would restore exactly the bug #789 removed.

Prefer a CSS variant over a resize listener — the collision is a width question, and the panel is already rendered. Hiding it with max-lg:hidden while a card is open costs no listener and no state; lg (1024px) is slightly conservative against the ~964px collision point, which is the safe direction. activeFeature is untouched, so clearing detail brings the panel straight back with its section, query and scroll position intact.

Do not change the card, its content, or infoCardHidden — the embedded constraint stays exactly as it is (R48).

Tests

The existing panel tests render SearchAreaPanel alone, so this belongs with the overlay's own layout rather than there. At minimum assert the class is applied only when a card is open, so the panel is not silently unreachable on a phone with nothing selected — that failure mode is worse than the bug.

Notes

Only reachable because Search now has a left-hand panel worth covering, so there is nothing to regress against development.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

issues.display_title: Issue #860: fix(editor): detect rooms as cycles in the wall graph, not regions in a raster
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-860-rooms-are-faces.mp4

Follow-up to #849, which made room detection resolve a room that is small next to its plan by reframing — a second raster pass over each closed wall group that the plan-wide pass left empty. That shipped and it is what unblocked the reported mall (level 1 47 → 245 of 269 Areas convertible, level 2 56 → 389 of 401).

Two things it deliberately did not fix. Both are the same raster, and both end with the same change, so they are one task rather than two.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Gap 1 — a small room inside a large connected wall network is still missed

The reframe pass keys on connected wall groups (closedWallGroups, src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/rooms.ts), and skips any group whose bounding box already contains a room the plan-wide pass found. That is correct for the shape the reported project has: separate footprints that touch nothing.

It buys nothing when the walls all touch. A plan drawn as one connected network — interior walls sharing endpoints with the outline, which is how a hand-drawn floor and many imports look — is a single group whose bbox is the whole floor, and the whole floor already has rooms in it. So the group is skipped and a kiosk-sized loop inside it stays invisible, exactly as before #849.

Gap 2 — detection cost grows with walls × rooms

wallsOnPolygon (rooms.ts:399) runs once per detected region, and inside it walks every tessellated wall chord × 3 samples × every polygon edge:

chords.forEach((w, ci) => { ... for (const tt of [0.15, 0.5, 0.85]) { ... for (let i = 0; i < poly.length; i++) { ... } } });

So detectRooms is O(regions × walls × edges), and recomputeRooms calls it on every model change — every drag, every wall edit. At ~4000 walls it is ~2.8 s per call. This is no longer theoretical: converting the Areas on 23839d5f-5390-45e8-9cb1-3109bf7d65d8 pushes that model to ~5100 walls, so #849 made this the next wall the same project hits.

Scope

Detect rooms as cycles in the wall graph instead of regions in a raster — direction 2 as written in #849, now with the reframe in place as the fallback to compare against.

  • Build the planar graph of wall segments: nodes = endpoints and crossings (snapped on the same tolerance closedWallGroups already uses), edges = the segments between them.
  • Rooms = the minimal faces of that graph, outer face excluded.
  • The cycle is the room polygon, so wallHugPolygon, simplify and wallsOnPolygon all retire — they exist only to undo raster error — and wallIdx falls out of the cycle's own edges instead of being re-derived by proximity.

That kills gap 1 outright (a cycle has no resolution) and gap 2 with it (O(E log E), no per-region wall sweep). Keep the reframe until the graph pass is proven on real data, then delete it.

Must not regress

detectRooms output feeds room polygons, 3D extrusion, the persisted level (modelToLevel), and the map/preview surfaces. Two identity rules constrain it hard:

  • r.key = d:${Math.round(cx)}:${Math.round(cy)} carries each room's height — a centroid that shifts loses it.
  • areaMeta in recomputeRooms is keyed by array position, so detected-room ordering is load-bearing too.

Existing plans must come out with the same rooms, the same polygons and the same order, or the change needs a migration. Verify on a saved house-scale project before and after.

Two behaviour changes to decide on rather than discover:

  • Any isolated closed loop becomes a Room — a column drawn as a box, a furniture outline — where the raster swallowed it under the 12-cell floor.
  • Nested loops (a room inside a room, an Area ring drawn inside a hall) need an explicit rule for which face wins.

Tests

src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/__tests__/rooms.test.ts holds the detection cases, including the #849 mall-scale ones.

  • Every existing case stays green with identical polygons and ordering.
  • A kiosk-sized loop sharing a wall with the mall outline is detected (gap 1 — extend the #849 fixture so the loop is not its own group).
  • A plan of ~4000 walls detects in well under the current ~2.8 s (guard the regression, not an exact number).
  • Convert To Room succeeds on the Areas of 23839d5f-5390-45e8-9cb1-3109bf7d65d8 that still refuse today.

pnpm test / pnpm lint / pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

RESULT

Branch: feature/860-wall-graph-rooms · PR: #863 (merged into development) · Commit: 10a62f6 · Merge: f4e1787

Direction taken: the wall-graph rewrite, as scoped. The reframe pass #849 added is gone with the raster it framed.

What shipped

Rooms are the minimal faces of the planar graph the walls form. Wall chords are cut at every crossing and T-junction, dangling chains are stripped, and each bounded face is a room. Nothing is sampled, so nothing depends on resolution, and the face IS the polygon — already on the wall centrelines, so wallHugPolygon, snapPolyToWalls and wallsOnPolygon retired with the raster they existed to correct.

Doors and windows join the graph as edges that are not walls, and only where they stand IN one (collinear with a wall they meet end to end). A Mappedin export cuts its wall at each doorway, leaving the room open; the opening in that gap is what says the room continues across it. A door drawn across a room contributes nothing.

Both gaps this task named are closed:

  • Gap 1 — a kiosk built against the mall outline, sharing its wall, is detected. There is no group to reframe and no resolution to run out of.
  • Gap 2 — wallsOnPolygon's O(regions × walls × edges) sweep is gone; wallIdx falls out of the face's own edges.

Identity, which detection improving at all depended on

before now
stored area → room k-th room to k-th area matched by geometry, positional only for the leftovers
containment probe polygonAreaAndCenter (vertex mean) interiorPoint
room height key exact d:round(cx):round(cy), a miss silently defaulted moved onto the room's current key once, at load

Two of those were live bugs, not hardening. On the mall import 24 of 25 Information links were lost on the first round-trip, because positional pairing sheared the moment detection resolved one room more. And a U-shaped room means to a point in its own notch, so the mean-based probe said the U was the room standing in the notch — the two swapped ids, links and types on every save, back and forth, on geometry nobody touched.

Effect, on the reported project 23839d5f-5390-45e8-9cb1-3109bf7d65d8

Converting every Area in turn, so the walls accumulate the way they do for the user:

before #848 after #849 now
level 1 convertible 16 / 269 245 / 269 267 / 269
level 2 convertible 0 / 401 389 / 401 400 / 401
detectRooms level 1 (4.9k walls) — 3395 ms 92 ms
detectRooms level 2 (8.2k walls) — 5425 ms 182 ms

The remaining refusals are rings that genuinely cross themselves (one per level) plus one face thinner than the node tolerance. The raster's own detectRooms on the same input answered 130 and 156 rooms; this answers 296 and 565.

Deliberate behaviour changes

  • Room.area is the exact polygon area — a few percent above the flood fill's inset, which stopped at the wall band. Surfaced in the m² readout and toGeoJSON.
  • A closed loop is a room at any size. The 12-cell floor was a raster limit, not a rule.
  • A face thinner than the tolerance at which two points count as the same point is the gap between two walls that should have been one, not a room.
  • A ring left open by more than a unit with no opening across it is honestly open. The raster's dilation used to close such a gap by accident — three cells, over a hundred units on a mall plan and two on a house plan.

Review

Two adversarial passes. A differential fuzz over 1 693 connected random rectilinear plans against an independent flood-fill oracle matched exactly; 3 500 random arbitrary-segment plans across four scales produced no throw, no NaN and no overlapping faces. Every finding was fixed on the branch:

  • blocker — the vertex-mean probe above.
  • major — an opening not standing in a wall manufactured a face (samples/edited_floorplan.4.txt came back with 11 rooms instead of 8).
  • major — a wedge between a wall drawn twice survived; now filtered on width.
  • minor — node fusing was order-dependent; it takes the nearest node now, so the answer does not depend on the order walls are stored in.
  • minor — a face reaching an island along a partition walked out and back, leaving a zero-width slit in the ring. The excursion is dropped from the outline; its walls stay in wallIdx.

Left standing, on purpose — raised as their own tasks

  • #864 — areaMeta is still keyed by array position. Correct on load (the pairing is geometric), but a room drawn mid-session that sorts into the middle still shifts every later room's type and colour by one seat.
  • #865 — converting every Area of an import leaves small faces where two rings nearly coincide. They are what the walls enclose; the fix belongs where the duplicate wall is created.

Tests

src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/__tests__/rooms.test.ts — a kiosk built against the mall outline; a hall split on a partition that ends mid-wall; a doorway closed by the door standing in it; a door that is not in a wall closing nothing; a dangling partition kept out of the polygon and inside the room; a doorway and a far-side partition not becoming corners; no slit where a partition ties an island to the wall; the same answer whatever order the walls are stored in; no wedge between a wall drawn twice; room type taken from the side the room is on; 900 rooms / 1 860 walls under the time bound.

src/lib/floorplanEditor/__tests__/roundtrip-area-link.test.ts — a concave room keeps its own identity across three round-trips (fails without the interior-point probe); the link survives a reordered previous list instead of being dropped.
src/lib/floorplanEditor/__tests__/roundtrip-area-link.int.test.ts — no link lands on a different polygon, and none may go missing, on the real Mappedin export.
src/lib/floorplanEditor/__tests__/bridge.test.ts — a room height whose key shifted is moved across, an exact key is left alone, and an ambiguous one is not guessed at.
src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/convert-area-to-room.test.ts — an Area the old raster was too coarse to see now converts.

pnpm test 1963 passed (3 skipped) · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean · pnpm lint 0 errors (11 warnings, all pre-existing in .playwright-mcp/demo).

Demo

.playwright-mcp/demo/860/video-860-rooms-are-faces.mp4 (60 fps, 2:51), recorded against the running app on duplicates of two real projects:

  1. A house plan, 1242 units across. A 24-unit kiosk is built against a wall it shares — one connected run of walls, which is the case #849's reframe could never reach. Rooms 7 → 8. The old grid gave the whole plan 300 cells, four units each, so it enclosed nothing that grid could see.
  2. The mall this was reported on, 23 597 units across. 269 tenants drawn as Areas, one Room. WOW! Mobile Boutique, Tbooth Wireless (kiosk) and Mobile Care (kiosk) — 2.75 m of shopfront each — convert one after another. Areas 269 → 266, Rooms 1 → 4, and not one "couldn't build a room from this area".

The scenario asserts each of those counts, so 860/dry.mjs fails the moment any of it stops being true.

In main via #866 (db0398a).

issues.display_title: Issue #861: fix(editor): undo after Convert To Room leaves the Area unlinked — the Information link is a store write no snapshot covers (#839)
issues.main_description_html:
Follow-up to #839 (PR #845), which shipped Convert To Room. PRD requirement R39 — "Convert To Room is reversible through undo" — is only half met, and the gap was declared rather than discovered: PR #845's own "left out, deliberately" section names it, and SelectionToolbars.tsx carries the ceiling as a ponytail: comment.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

Convert an Area that is linked to an Information record, then Ctrl+Z.

The Area comes back with its geometry and its name — both live in the engine's JSON snapshot (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/history.ts:10) — but not its Information link. The Room that held the link is gone with its walls, so the link is on nothing: the Information record survives, as the PRD requires, but is orphaned, and the user has to re-link by hand with no sign that anything was dropped.

Why

infoId is a store field, not an engine field. EngineModel["manualAreas"] (src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts:42) carries id, name, points, createdAt and nothing else, so the engine's snapshot cannot capture the link and undo() cannot restore it.

The link survives an ordinary round-trip only because modelToLevel re-attaches it from the previous store level, by id:

const pa = prevAreaById.get(m.id);
return { ...pa, id: m.id, ... };   // bridge.ts:307-317

Conversion breaks that chain. convertAreaToRoom splices the Area out of model.manualAreas (editor/commands.ts:265), so the next modelToLevel emits no row for it and the store row disappears; convertToRoom in SelectionToolbars.tsx:120-124 then calls setAreaInfo(room.id, prevInfoId) to put the link on the new Room. One undo later the Room's row is gone and the Area's id is no longer in prevAreaById, so pa === undefined and the restored Area has no infoId to spread.

The ceiling already recorded, and why it is not simply lifted

SelectionToolbars.tsx:104-108 names the upgrade path — an infoId slot on model.areaMeta carried through metaOf — and rejects it because "a present areaMeta key beats the pairing guard and would reintroduce #798".

That objection is correct for detected Rooms and needs re-reading rather than repeating. metaOf is called with a positional key on the detected path (metaOf(String(rawIndex), pa), bridge.ts:377) and its result is spread after the #798-guarded ...carried, so any field it returns from pa bypasses pairingHolds — which is exactly the bug #798 fixed. For manual Areas the same helper is called with m:${m.id} (bridge.ts:321), which is id-keyed and carries no positional hazard.

So the fix has to distinguish the two call sites rather than extend metaOf blindly.

Scope

Make the Information link survive undo (and redo) of a Convert To Room, without letting any store-only field bypass the #798 pairing guard on the detected-room path.

Two facts that shape it, both verified:

  • snapshot() already includes areaMeta and restore() already puts it back (history.ts:10, history.ts:117) — an id-keyed carrier there rides undo for free.
  • ctx.on.historyStep?.("undo" | "redo") already exists as a hook (editor/context.ts:63), currently used only for analytics (FloorplanEditor.tsx:398). Whether that or the model carrier is the right seam is the implementation call.

The store row's presence, not its infoId value, has to decide whether any fallback is consulted: an Area the user deliberately unlinked has a row with infoId: undefined, and a ?? fallback would resurrect the old link.

Acceptance

  • Convert a linked Area to a Room, undo — the Area is back, still linked to the same Information record, and the Information panel shows it linked.
  • Redo — the link is back on the Room.
  • Unlink an Area, convert it, undo — the Area comes back unlinked; no stale link resurrects.
  • Convert an unlinked Area, undo — no link appears from anywhere.
  • The #798 guard still holds: an edit that reorders detected rooms does not move an Information link onto unrelated geometry, and existing #798 coverage stays green.
  • Undo across a page reload behaves the same as in-session, or the difference is stated in code (fp_history: mirrors the stacks to localStorage).
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #862: feat(editor): add and remove a vertex on an Area (#839)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-862-area-vertex.mp4

Follow-up to #839 (PR #845). PRD R22 — "Areas can be reshaped by vertex editing" (Must) — shipped as move only. The PRD asks for more:

Vertex editing must support moving existing vertices. It should also support adding and removing vertices when the local editor interaction pattern can do so without introducing an unsafe shortcut. — prd.md:175

Adding or removing vertices should use the same style of explicit handle or action used elsewhere in the editor where possible. — prd.md:382

PR #845 left it out with the reason "the editor has no precedent for the gesture". That is the task: survey the editor's existing geometry gestures, pick the one that fits, and build it.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What exists today

ctx.areaDrag = { i, handle } (editor/context.ts:205). A pointerdown on a vertex handle sets handle and the pointermove branch writes that one point; a pointerdown on the body sets handle: null and translates the whole ring (editor/interactions.ts:284-290, 366-370, 478-495). pushUndo fires once per gesture, gated on DRAG_MIN and ctx.committed, so a drag is exactly one undo step.

There is no way to add a vertex and no way to remove one. An Area drawn or imported with the wrong number of corners can only be deleted and redrawn — which also loses its name and its Information link.

Scope

  • Add a vertex on an Area edge.
  • Remove a vertex from an Area.
  • Both follow an affordance the editor already uses, rather than a new invention. Survey first — wall point editing, the Area draw tool's own point handling, shape handles, curve handles, the canvas context-menu path used by openRename (interactions.ts:630) — then choose, and say in code why.
  • One undo step per action.

Guards

  • Never below 3 vertices — the PRD's floor for an Area, and convertAreaToRoom refuses under it anyway (commands.ts:225).
  • The result must stay a simple polygon. isSimplePolygon (floorplan/geometry.ts:413) is what Convert To Room validates with, so a reshape that crosses itself makes the Area unconvertible — refuse or revert rather than commit it.
  • An added vertex must not land on top of a neighbour: ringCorners (geometry.ts:405) collapses zero-length edges, so a duplicate point silently disappears on the next conversion.
  • Editors only. The Viewer role must not get the affordance.

Acceptance

  • A vertex can be added to an Area edge, and the Area's shape follows it.
  • A vertex can be removed from an Area.
  • The gesture matches an affordance already used elsewhere in this editor; if none fits, the chosen one is justified in code.
  • Each action is a single undo step, and redo restores it.
  • An Area cannot be reduced below 3 vertices.
  • A change that would make the ring self-intersect is refused and the Area is left unchanged.
  • The Area stays convertible after editing — Convert To Room still succeeds on the reshaped ring.
  • Read-only / Viewer mode shows no add or remove affordance.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #870: fix(editor): the empty-project tip is an invisible shield over the drawing tools (#868)
issues.main_description_html:
Reported in #868 — after Create an empty project, the drawing tools in the editor cannot be selected. Clicking Wall, Door, Window, Area, Shapes, Point or Safety does nothing at all: no active state, no cursor change, no status line.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

The "Start with the outer walls" tip (EmptyCanvasPointer, #452) is mounted but never positioned, and an unpositioned card is an invisible click shield lying on top of the tool row.

Its useLayoutEffect positions the card against #tool-add-wall:

const target = document.getElementById("tool-add-wall")
if (!surface || !target) return          // ← gives up, and never retries

On the empty-project arrival the Wall tool is not in the DOM yet. useEditorCapabilities() is deliberately pessimistic while projectAccess loads (integration pack §A5), so the editor renders a Viewer's toolbar first — no drawing tools at all — and only swaps in the full row once the role resolves. By then the effect has already returned, and its deps are [dismissed, hasGeometry, isEmptyFlow], none of which change when the role lands, so it never runs again.

The card is still rendered. positioned stays false, so it draws at opacity: 0 — but it keeps pointer-events-auto, z-30, and the untransformed bottom-0 left-0 of #editor-canvas-surface, while the tool row is bottom-12 at z-20. The two overlap.

Measured on a freshly created empty project (1920×1080, document.elementFromPoint over each button):

card: role=status  rect[296,958 → 632,1056]  opacity:0  z-index:30  pointer-events:auto
Add wall (W)               x=361  BLOCKED by the tip card
Add curve wall             x=395  BLOCKED
Add door (D)               x=429  BLOCKED
Add window (N)             x=463  BLOCKED
Add area (A)               x=497  BLOCKED
Shapes                     x=538  BLOCKED
Add point (P)              x=579  BLOCKED
Add safety annotation (S)  x=613  BLOCKED (by the card's own dismiss button)
Add access (L)             x=654  clickable
...everything from here on clickable

page.click("#tool-add-wall") fails with Timeout 5000ms exceeded — Playwright's "element intercepts pointer events".

That the tip is invisible is the same bug from the other side: the guidance #452 was built to show never appears on the flow it exists for.

Fix

  1. Move the surface/target lookup inside the rAF loop, so the card positions itself the moment the tool row appears instead of giving up on the first frame. This restores the tip and removes the shield.
  2. pointer-events: none while positioned is false — an invisible overlay must never take a click, whatever the reason it has not been placed.

Acceptance criteria

  • On a project created via Create an empty project, every drawing tool is clickable the moment the toolbar appears
  • The "Start with the outer walls" tip appears above the Wall tool on that flow
  • The tip still dismisses on the close button and on Escape, and stays dismissed
  • The tip still disappears once the floor has geometry
  • Regression test covering the toolbar-arrives-late ordering
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

RESULT

Root cause confirmed by reproduction, not by reading. The reported video was decoded frame by frame: at t=14s the URL still carries ?empty=1 and the toolbar is the Viewer's (six view controls, no drawing tools); from t=15s the full row is up, and from t=20s to t=27s the pointer sits on the Wall tool, clicking, with the button never entering its active state.

Reproduced on a freshly created empty project at 1920x1080 by asking the DOM what actually receives each click:

card: role=status  rect[296,958 - 632,1056]  opacity:0  z-index:30  pointer-events:auto
Add wall (W)               x=361  BLOCKED by the tip card
Add curve wall             x=395  BLOCKED
Add door (D)               x=429  BLOCKED
Add window (N)             x=463  BLOCKED
Add area (A)               x=497  BLOCKED
Shapes                     x=538  BLOCKED
Add point (P)              x=579  BLOCKED
Add safety annotation (S)  x=613  BLOCKED (by the card's own dismiss button)
Add access (L)             x=654  clickable  ... and everything after it

click("#tool-add-wall") failed with Timeout 5000ms exceeded — the element intercepts pointer events. After the fix all 19 buttons report blockedBy: null and the Wall tool reports aria-pressed="true" on click.

What was wrong

EmptyCanvasPointer positions itself against #tool-add-wall, which is not in the DOM when an empty project first opens: useEditorCapabilities is pessimistic while projectAccess loads, so the editor renders a Viewer's tool row first. The useLayoutEffect looked the button up once and returned; its deps are [dismissed, hasGeometry, isEmptyFlow], so it never ran again when the role landed. The card stayed mounted and unpositioned — opacity: 0, but pointer-events-auto, z-30, at the untransformed bottom-0 left-0 of the canvas surface, on top of a tool row at bottom-12, z-20.

The tip never appearing is the same bug from the other side: the guidance #452 exists for was invisible on the one flow it was built for.

What changed

src/components/editor/EmptyCanvasPointer.tsx

  1. The surface and the button are looked up inside the rAF loop, so the card places itself the moment the tool row arrives.
  2. Visibility rides with the position, imperatively, instead of living in React state. A positioned state outlives the node — React drops the card as soon as the floor has geometry, and undoing that first wall brought it back with the state still true and the transform gone with the old node: opaque, clickable, in the wrong corner. The card now renders hidden and inert and is only switched on where the transform is written, so a remount is always safe.
  3. The geometry effect persisted "dismissed" without setting the state, so an undo re-showed a tip the project was already done with and only a reload honoured the write. It is also what made (2) reachable.
  4. The loop gives up after ~10s of misses: a real Viewer's tool row has no drawing tools at all, so the lookup can never succeed for them and the poll would otherwise outlive the tab.

src/components/editor/__tests__/EmptyCanvasPointer.lateToolbar.test.tsx — new, 6 cases: inert while it has nowhere to point; placed over the Wall tool once the row arrives; clamped at the edge instead of hanging off it; the poll really stops on unmount; giving up on a row that never arrives; and coming back inert rather than opaque when geometry is undone. Five of the six fail against the code on development, and the placement assertion was mutation-tested — swapping renderedWidth / 2 for renderedWidth turns it red.

Four adversarial reviewers went over the first version of this fix; the stale-positioned remount, the clamp-dominated placement assertion, the unbounded poll and the weak unmount assertion above all came from that pass and are fixed here.

Verification

  • pnpm test — 214 files, 1992 passed, 3 skipped
  • pnpm exec tsc --noEmit — clean
  • pnpm lint — 0 errors (13 pre-existing warnings, none in these files)
  • Browser: empty project created through the real flow on :6060; every tool clickable, tip visible above the Wall tool, Wall activates on click

Commit: 6bd302f

Demo

.playwright-mcp/demo/868/video-868-tools-take-clicks.mp4 (60 fps, 1:42), recorded against the running app on a project created through the real Create an empty project flow — no existing project is touched.

  1. The project is created from the dashboard and the editor opens on one blank floor.
  2. The tip appears, pointing at the Wall tool. The scenario fails if its computed opacity is not 1 — that guidance was invisible on this flow, and the invisible card IS what was eating the clicks.
  3. Every button in the tool row is put to document.elementFromPoint: whatever answers at each button's centre must be that button. Eight used to answer with the tip card; the scenario throws if any still does.
  4. The Wall tool takes the click (aria-pressed="true" is asserted), four walls are drawn, Room 1 is detected, and the tip retires now the floor has geometry.
